body.p: Claims 1, 3-8, 10-16, and 23-28 are pending, of which claims 1, 3, 8, and 12 are amended. Support for the amendments can be found throughout the application as filed, including at least in paragraphs [0054]-[0055] and the originally-filed claims. No new matter is added by this amendment. This Amendment is being made solely to expedite prosecution of this application and does not constitute an acquiescence to any prior art or rejections identified by the Examiner.
Claims 1, 3-8, 10-16, and 23-28 are rejected under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. §102(a)(1) and §102(a)(2) as allegedly being anticipated by US 2012/0265037 to Bohm et al. ("Bohm"). See Office Action at 5.

To reject claims in an application under § 102, the Office Action must establish that each and every claim feature is present within the four corners of a single reference. "A claim is anticipated only if each and every element as set forth in the claim is found, either expressly or inherently described, in a single prior art reference." MPEP § 2131 (quoting Verdegaal Bros. v. Union Oil Co. of California, 814 F.2d 628, 631, 2 USPQ2d 1051, 1053 (Fed. Cir. 1987)). Further, "the elements must be arranged as required by the claim[.]" Id. (citing In re Bond, 910 F.2d 831, 15 USPQ2d 1566 (Fed. Cir. 1990)). As discussed below, Applicant respectfully submits Bohm does not disclose or suggest each and every feature of claims 1, 3-8, 10-16, and 23-28.
Bohm does not disclose or suggest a glucose monitoring system including, among other

features, "obtaining, by the processing circuity, a shelf duration of the analyte sensor; adjusting, by the processing circuitry, processing of the sensor data to compensate for the shelf duration adjusting the slope associated with the sensitivity of the analyte sensor; determining, by the processing circuitry, the level of the analyte of the user from the sensor data using the adjusted slope" as recited in claim 1. The Office Action cites to paragraph [0406] of Bohm as allegedly disclosing the shelf duration as claimed. Bohm, however, merely describes calibration process 2400 can use one or more pre-implant information 2402, including time since sensor manufacture. See Bohm, paragraphs [0398]-[0406]. Bohm does not disclose or suggest

"obtaining, by the processing circuity, a shelf duration of the analyte sensor" and "adjusting, by the processing circuitry, processing of the sensor data to compensate for the shelf duration adjusting the slope associated with the sensitivity of the analyte sensor." Furthermore, paragraph [0274] of Bohm describes a conversion function including y representing the sensor signal and m (the slope) representing the sensor sensitivity. Bohm does not disclose or suggest, at least, "adjusting, by the processing circuitry, processing of the sensor data to compensate for the shelf duration adjusting the slope associated with the sensitivity of the analyte sensor," let alone "determining, by the processing circuitry, the level of the analyte of the user from the sensor data using the adjusted slope" as recited in claim 1.
Accordingly, Applicant submits independent claim 1 is not anticipated by Bohm. Dependent Claims 3-8, 10-16, and 23-28

Claims 3-8, 10-16, and 23-28 depend, directly or indirectly, from independent claim 1. Applicant, therefore, respectfully submits that claims 3-8, 10-16, and 23-28 are allowable at least based on their dependence from allowable independent claim 1. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests that the rejections of claims 3-8, 10-16, and 23-28 under 35 U.S.C. § 102 be

On the basis of the foregoing remarks, Applicant respectfully submits that the pending claims of this application are allowable over the art of record. Applicant thus respectfully requests the previous rejections be withdrawn, and that the pending claims be allowed by the Examiner. Favorable consideration and timely allowance of this application are respectfully requested.

The above remarks are made solely to expedite prosecution of this application and do not constitute an acquiescence to any reference identified or rejection raised by the Office Action. Applicant believes that a full and complete reply has been made to the outstanding Office Action and, as such, the present application is in condition for allowance. Applicant thus respectfully requests the previous rejections be withdrawn, and that the pending claims be allowed by the Examiner. Favorable consideration and timely allowance of this application are respectfully requested.
